summary.text: Veronica Escobar is the Democratic incumbent seeking re-election to Texas's 16th District. A third-generation El Pasoan, she taught English, ran a nonprofit, and served as El Paso County Commissioner and County Judge before winning the seat in 2018. She serves on the House Appropriations and Budget committees in the 119th Congress (2025-2026).

paragraphs.text: Born in El Paso, Texas, in 1969. Her official biography describes her as a third-generation El Pasoan.
Graduated from the University of Texas at El Paso and New York University; Ballotpedia lists a bachelor's degree in 1991 and a master's degree in English Literature in 1993.

Before elected office, taught English at the University of Texas at El Paso and El Paso Community College, served as communications director for former El Paso Mayor Raymond Caballero, and was executive director of Community Scholars, a nonprofit that taught high school students to produce public policy reports.

Served as an El Paso County Commissioner from 2006 to 2010 and as El Paso County Judge from 2011 to 2017. Her official biography says she worked with University Medical Center of El Paso to build primary care clinics and the El Paso Children's Hospital.

Won the Democratic primary and the November 6, 2018 general election for the open seat previously held by Beto O'Rourke, defeating Republican Rick Seeberger; took office in 2019. Her official biography says she was the first woman elected to represent El Paso in Congress.

In earlier terms she served on the House Judiciary, Armed Services, and Ethics committees; she now serves on Appropriations (with Budget in the 119th Congress). In the 118th Congress she was one of three co-chairs of the Democratic Policy and Communications Committee.

Her official biography lists membership in the Congressional Hispanic Caucus, Congressional Progressive Caucus, New Democrat Coalition, Democratic Women's Caucus, and Pro-Choice Caucus, and describes her legislative work on immigration, gun safety, health care, and reproductive health clinic security.
According to her official biography, she lives in Central El Paso with her husband, Michael; they have two grown children.
